overview: EQT Corporation is the largest natural gas producer in the United States and the country's only large-scale, vertically integrated natural gas company, with upstream, gathering and transmission operations concentrated in the Marcellus and Utica shales of the Appalachian Basin. Following its 2024 acquisition of Equitrans Midstream, EQT now owns both the wells that produce the gas and much of the pipeline infrastructure that gathers and transports it, allowing the company to capture margin across the value chain rather than just at the wellhead. The company operates roughly 2.3 million gross acres, holds about 28 Tcfe of proved reserves, and is increasingly positioning itself as the supplier of choice for gas-fired power plants and data center/AI load growth in the eastern US.

business_model.summary: EQT makes money primarily by producing and selling natural gas (plus associated NGLs and oil) from its Marcellus/Utica acreage, and since the 2024 Equitrans Midstream acquisition, also earns fee-based gathering and transmission revenue for moving its own and third-party gas through its owned pipeline network. The upstream business is commodity-price-sensitive and largely hedged/marketed by EQT's own commercial function; the midstream (gathering/transmission) business is more annuity-like, generating relatively stable cash flow through commodity cycles. EQT is increasingly signing long-term, price-linked supply agreements directly with power generators, data center developers and LNG offtakers, shifting a portion of volumes away from spot/basis-exposed sales toward contracted, premium-priced demand.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - utilities, power generators, industrial users, LNG exporters, and gas marketers; increasingly direct long-term contracts with data center/power developers (e.g., CPV, Homer City Redevelopment) and an Asian LNG offtaker
business_model.geographic_mix: Essentially 100% domestic US operations concentrated in the Appalachian Basin (Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Ohio); gas is sold into Northeast/Mid-Atlantic markets, the Gulf Coast (via transport capacity and LNG-linked deals), and increasingly directly to in-basin power/data center demand

competitive_position.market_position: Largest natural gas producer in the US by volume and the only large-scale, vertically integrated (upstream + midstream) natural gas company in the country, giving it structural cost and optionality advantages versus pure-play E&Ps in the same basin

moat_factors.description: Ownership of gathering and transmission infrastructure (via Equitrans Midstream acquisition) lets EQT control takeaway capacity, capture midstream margin, and reduce basis/curtailment risk that pure E&P peers face
Marcellus core-county wells have among the lowest breakeven costs in North America (sub-$1.50/MMBtu in core areas), aided by long laterals and combo-development pad drilling

2.3 million gross acres, ~2,945 miles of pipeline, and deep drilling inventory support decades of low-cost development and give EQT the scale to sign the largest single-site gas supply contracts in North America (e.g., Homer City 4.4 GW campus)
First-mover position signing 10-year power/data-center supply deals (CPV, Homer City) and LNG offtake agreements gives revenue visibility and pricing uplift versus spot Appalachian basis

Aggressive post-merger debt paydown (net debt down to $5.5B from $7.7B at YE2025) supports credit rating upgrades (S&P revised outlook to positive) and lower cost of capital versus more leveraged peers

weaknesses: Single-basin (Appalachian) and single-commodity (natural gas) concentration leaves EQT more exposed to regional basis and Appalachian-specific regulatory/pipeline risk than diversified peers
Still elevated leverage from the ~$5.5B Equitrans Midstream acquisition, even after paydown, versus historically low-leverage pure E&Ps
Integration and realization of remaining merger synergies (target $425M+, ~$360M captured as of 2025) carries execution risk
Midstream segment introduces regulatory/permitting risk (e.g., pipeline projects like MVP Southgate) that upstream-only peers don't carry
Natural gas price volatility remains the dominant swing factor in earnings despite hedging and contracted volumes

growth_drivers: Power generation and data center/AI demand growth — long-term contracted supply deals such as the 10-year CPV Shay Energy Center agreement (325,000 Dth/d) and the Homer City Redevelopment 4.4 GW AI/HPC campus deal (up to 665,000 MMBtu/d) provide premium, PJM-linked pricing versus in-basin gas prices

LNG export exposure — 5-year, 0.5 million tonnes/year offtake agreement with a large Asian energy company beginning 2028, expected to add ~$45 million to 2028 free cash flow, with potential for additional LNG-linked deals as US export capacity grows
Continued Equitrans Midstream synergy capture — additional cost synergies beyond the ~$360 million already realized toward the $425 million+ target
MVP Southgate completion (targeted year-end 2026) and other pipeline buildout, expanding takeaway capacity and southeast market access
Bolt-on M&A in midstream/downstream adjacencies (e.g., $77 million Blackline Midstream propane storage/distribution acquisition, ~20% FCF yield) to deepen vertical integration
Operational efficiency gains — longer laterals, combo-development, and compression investments have repeatedly pushed production above guidance while capex has come in below guidance
Balance sheet deleveraging toward the ~$5.0 billion long-term debt target, which should lower interest expense and support further capital returns (dividends, $2B buyback authorization)

business.description: Revenue and cash flow are highly sensitive to natural gas prices, which averaged just $2.89/MMBtu in Q2 2026; sustained low prices pressure margins and capital returns despite hedging
Nearly all production and infrastructure is in the Appalachian Basin, exposing EQT to regional basis differentials, takeaway constraints, and Appalachia-specific weather/regulatory events

Large long-dated supply agreements (CPV, Homer City) depend on counterparties' power plants and data centers being built on schedule (Homer City targeted 2027, CPV facility as early as 2031); delays or cancellations would push out expected cash flow benefits

financial.description: Net debt of $5.5 billion (down from $7.7B at YE2025) still requires continued paydown to reach the ~$5.0 billion long-term target; commodity downturns could slow deleveraging
Derivative/hedging positions used to manage price risk can require margin postings and can cap upside in strong price environments
Debt-funded acquisition activity leaves EQT sensitive to refinancing costs if rates remain elevated

regulatory.description: Midstream buildout (e.g., MVP Southgate) requires federal/state permits and is subject to legal challenges and environmental review that can delay projects and raise costs

regulatory.risk: Federal and state energy/climate policy shifts
regulatory.description: Changes in methane regulation, emissions rules, or federal leasing/permitting policy could raise compliance costs or affect development pace
As a large-scale driller and pipeline operator, EQT faces ongoing risk of environmental, royalty, and property-related litigation

macro.description: Gas prices are driven by weather, storage levels, and broader energy market dynamics largely outside EQT's control; the stock's earnings and multiple are highly correlated with the Henry Hub/Appalachian basis price cycle

The bull thesis increasingly depends on continued AI/data-center-driven electricity demand growth; a slowdown in data center buildout or a shift toward alternative power sources (renewables, nuclear) would reduce the incremental demand EQT is counting on
US LNG export capacity additions (and thus incremental demand pull on Appalachian gas) depend on macro trade, permitting, and global gas demand trends outside EQT's control

macro_factors.industry_outlook: US natural gas demand is expected to grow meaningfully over the next several years, driven by LNG export capacity additions, coal-to-gas power switching, and a new wave of gas-fired power generation to serve data center/AI electricity load growth. Appalachian producers with vertical integration and infrastructure access (like EQT) are positioned to capture premium, longer-duration contracts as generators and data center developers seek firm, reliable supply.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — natural gas prices are cyclical and weather/storage-driven; EQT's upstream earnings swing materially with Henry Hub and Appalachian basis prices, though the midstream (gathering/transmission) segment and growing contracted-demand book provide a more stable earnings floor than a pure E&P peer
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — capital-intensive drilling and midstream buildout, plus meaningful debt load from the Equitrans acquisition, make EQT sensitive to borrowing costs, though an improving credit rating (S&P outlook revised to positive) is reducing this sensitivity over time
key_input_costs: Drilling and completion services/oilfield services costs
Steel/tubular goods for well construction and pipelines

recent_developments.event: Reported Q2 2026 results: sales volume of 634 Bcfe beat the high end of guidance; EPS of $0.39 missed consensus ($0.42) while revenue of $1.81B slightly beat; free cash flow of $330M; capex 9% below low end of guidance; net debt improved to $5.5B from $7.7B at YE2025
Raised full-year 2026 production guidance by ~90 Bcfe to 2,375-2,450 Bcfe on strong well performance and compression investments; trimmed full-year capex guidance by $25 million
Closed the $77 million Blackline Midstream acquisition, adding propane storage and distribution terminals in New England at an estimated ~20% free cash flow yield

Signed a 10-year gas supply agreement with Competitive Power Ventures (CPV) to supply 325,000 Dth/d to the planned 2-GW CPV Shay Energy Center in West Virginia, with pricing linked to PJM power markets
Signed a 5-year LNG offtake agreement with a large Asian energy company for 0.5 million tonnes/year beginning 2028, expected to add ~$45 million to 2028 free cash flow

Announced agreement in principle with Homer City Redevelopment to be the exclusive natural gas supplier (up to 665,000 MMBtu/d) for a planned 4.4 GW natural gas-fired power facility serving a 3,200-acre AI/HPC data center campus in Pennsylvania — one of the largest single-site gas supply arrangements in North American history
Exercised preferential buy-out rights to acquire additional interests in Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP A and MVP C) for ~$200.7 million and ~$12.5 million respectively
Completed Olympus Energy acquisition, adding 1,768 Bcfe of proved reserves and expanding the upstream base

Continued to capture Equitrans Midstream merger synergies — approximately $360 million of the $425 million+ target realized by 2025 — and continued aggressive debt paydown (over $8.1 billion repaid since the 2024 merger closed), prompting S&P to revise EQT's outlook from stable to positive while affirming BBB- rating

Sell-side analysts have been raising price targets through September 2026 (e.g., UBS to $77 from $73, Citi to $68 from $67), reflecting increased confidence in the data center/power demand and deleveraging story; consensus is Moderate Buy with average target around $68 versus a share price near $52

items.notes: Reduced by $25 million versus prior guidance on operational efficiency gains; Q2 capex came in 9% below the low end of guidance
Quarterly guide issued alongside Q2 results
34-50 net wells to be completed in Q3 2026

items.target: Approximately $1.03/Mcfe (Q2 2026 actual, at low end of guidance)
items.notes: Driven by lower-than-expected transmission, SG&A, and lease operating expenses
Net debt already down to $5.5 billion as of Q2 2026 from $7.7 billion at YE2025; target subject to commodity price environment
5% increase; supported by a $2 billion share repurchase authorization
All regulatory approvals secured; ~$85 million in accelerated capital contributions targeted to hit the year-end completion date

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Toby Rice emphasized that EQT has become 'the partner of choice in Appalachia,' leveraging scale, infrastructure footprint and commercial capabilities to capture an outsized share of power generation and data center demand growth. Management continues to frame strategy around generating durable free cash flow across commodity cycles, aggressive post-merger debt reduction toward the ~$5.0 billion target, and converting a growing share of production into long-term, premium-priced contracted volumes (CPV, Homer City, LNG offtake) rather than spot/basis-exposed sales.

bull_case: Only large-scale, vertically integrated natural gas producer in the US, giving EQT structural cost advantages and the ability to capture margin across upstream and midstream that pure-play E&P peers cannot

First-mover position on long-term, premium-priced supply contracts with power generators and data center/AI campuses (CPV, Homer City) provides multi-decade demand visibility at pricing above spot Appalachian basis

Aggressive deleveraging since the Equitrans Midstream merger (net debt down to $5.5B from $7.7B at YE2025, $8.1B+ repaid since 2024) is improving the credit profile (S&P outlook revised to positive) and freeing cash flow for buybacks/dividends
Repeated pattern of production beating guidance while capex comes in below guidance signals continued operational efficiency gains (longer laterals, compression investments, combo-development)

Structural tailwind from LNG export growth and electrification/AI-driven power demand should support Appalachian gas demand and pricing over the medium term, with EQT best positioned to capture it given its infrastructure scale
bear_case: Earnings remain highly levered to volatile natural gas prices (Q2 2026 realized only $2.89/MMBtu); a sustained low-price environment would pressure free cash flow and slow the deleveraging story

Single-basin (Appalachian), single-commodity (natural gas) concentration leaves EQT more exposed than diversified energy peers to regional basis blowouts, weather events, and Appalachia-specific regulatory/permitting risk

The bull case increasingly depends on data center/AI power demand materializing on schedule; delays or cancellations of large projects like Homer City (targeted 2027) or CPV Shay (as early as 2031) would push out the expected cash flow benefits investors are already pricing in
Leverage remains above historical pure-E&P norms following the ~$5.5B Equitrans Midstream acquisition, and full realization of the $425M+ synergy target is not yet complete

Stock has already re-rated with analyst price targets rising through September 2026 (consensus ~$68 vs. ~$52 share price), so much of the vertical-integration and demand-growth story may already be reflected in valuation, leaving less margin of safety if execution disappoints
